items.title: Node and relay split: the review of 2026-10-10
items.box:
WHAT: act on the review "SpiritOS relay and node split review" (Andreas Thut, 2026-10-10, at e8f8ffd, four parallel readers of relay.js whole and the node's wire path, repros of S1, S3, S6 on Node 22). Its summary: the relay keeps its envelope rule; the node breaks its own; both layers still carry app knowledge; the worst problems are trust, not layering: reply text is signed by nobody, and one member can lock the owner out of every relay verb. The three rules checked are NODE-AND-RELAY.md's: the relay carries, the node stores, the shell understands.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-10): "Greate a goal in desk for this". Items are added one at a time at his word (rule/7); every relay-wire change and every node verb change is a review-and-yes change.

CHECKED by claude-windows at b355e36d (the headline items, in the tree as the review says; the low items taken on the review's word until their item opens):
- S1: the receipt signs 'receipt', the REQUEST hash and the minute (relayAuth.js receiptMessage); the reply text is bound by nothing, and the seal is anonymous, so a relay can swap the text and the receipt still verifies.
- S2: deliverForwardedReply (relay.js) checks only that the partner's reply.from is the route's target, never reply.sig, then announceRoute tells every member where the key lives.
- S3: router.js DEFAULT_PER_TARGET is 1 and every self-addressed verb opens its route on the relay's own key: one slot for owner, member and partner verbs together.
- N1: server.js hands wire.decode as a value to four witnesses (puppetMode, apiDoor, ownerPost, boxes); each decodes every admitted arrival; nodeKnowsNoApps.js matches only the written call, and is red today (its control fails).
- N2: apiDoor.js refuses a body whose args.by is 'andy' and branches on app 'api'; the desk takes the writer from the caller now (writerOf), so the check guards nothing and refuses a member's search by 'andy'.
- A1: the node's relay list is shell/natter/relays.json (ownerBadge.js, hub.js, server.js, presenceNode.js), created with Andy's relay as default at every boot; the path is in error texts.
- R1: relayRequest.js and serveCommon.js build a body by string concatenation per chunk: a multi-byte character split across chunks becomes U+FFFD, a request then fails its signature, a reply changes unnoticed.

THE REVIEW'S FINDINGS, by rule (severity in brackets)
Rule 1, the relay opens only what is addressed to it: HOLDS. Around it: R1 chunk concatenation [medium]; R2 partner gate runs every verb in a body, not one [medium]; R3 a truthy card exempts a post from sealing and every verb in it runs, so an invite token can travel in plaintext [medium]; R4 the DEBUG monitor copies pass-through text to the owner, a decision of 2026-09-26 [low]; R5 sizes compared in UTF-16 units, Andy's ruling says bytes [low].
Rule 2, the node decodes the envelope and nothing inside: BROKEN. N1 [high]; N2 [high]; N3 peerPost refusalIn parses every reply without checking it is not an app's, so an app's {ok:false} is read as a node refusal and the card is re-fetched [medium]; N4 the node composes packets addressed to apps (published, api), which a puppet app can forge [medium]; N5 answerRelay and nodeCard parse inline before checking the sender, correct but unseen by the guard [low]. Held stranger: B1 a held packet is receipted as delivered [high]; B2 held text is logged and kept in memory forever, against the comment [medium].
Rule 3, no app logic in node or relay: BROKEN. A1 [high]; A2 = N2 [high]; A3 the error catalogue defines desk, deskClient, chatClerver and fileServer codes, and an app cannot define its own (define throws) [medium]; A4 per-peer stats written into the Contacts app's folder [medium]. Placement: hub reads Contacts' old prefs (expires at alpha); jobs/api.json describes a verb with the desk's shape; the relay refuses to start without shell and process folders it never loads; relayServer requires peerPost, which pulls contacts and node:sqlite onto a relay; bash http-to-https and RELAY-HOST tell operators a stale app/natter path.
Wire security: S1 [high, repro]; S2 [high]; S3 [high, repro]; S4 the rate limit is charged to the claimed sender before the signature is checked, so junk with a public key exhausts that member [medium]; S5 a sealed owner post can be replayed for about two minutes, seal.open's time is unchecked for self-addressed verbs [medium]; S6 a double device offer overwrites the awaiting slot and the first hangs [medium, repro]; S7 the onward budget is the requested one, not the 5 s granted, late forwards leak carrying entries [medium]; S8 a stream header names no relay and carries no nonce, so one relay can replay it on another within three minutes [medium]; S9 a post signed once is resent on retry and after restart, past the three-minute window, and 403 is final [medium]; S10 relayRequest has no socket timeout, no size cap, no error handler [medium]; S11 loopback servers subscribing as a page mark the backlog taken, so a closed browser loses waiting lines [medium]; S12 frontDoor never checks blocked under acquire [medium]; S13 claim rate limit keyed on remoteAddress behind Caddy, one bucket for everybody [medium, suspected]. Low: deviceOffer's 5 s ttl; seats missing from the owner's report; carry runs before size checks; peerPost adopts the wire's hash (against decision 0011); the relay identity written in place; one partner can fill all forward slots; card asks bypass the front door and log two rows each; under acquire a stranger is known after one message.
The guard: nodeKnowsNoApps.js misses a decode passed as a value, an inline parse, decorate, a branch on .app, and exempts kernel.js whole; a stronger guard bans client/packet from the node layer's requires but one named file, and flags any .app read on arrival text.

THE REVIEW'S ORDER, as proposed items (each at his word): 1 S1+S2 the receipt binds the reply text and a forwarded reply is verified before a route is announced; 2 S3 self-addressed verbs get their own capacity; 3 A1 the relay list leaves the Natter folder for node state behind a node verb; 4 N2 the 'andy' check and the app branch leave apiDoor; 5 N1 + the guard: one named decoder in the node layer and a guard that sees it; then R1, B1/B2, S4 to S13 and the rest in batches.
